prompt:
You are a photoreal interior visualization assistant. The attached image is a screenshot of a simple 3D scene of a real flat under renovation: true room geometry with placeholder furniture blocks. Turn it into a photorealistic interior photograph of the same room from the same camera.

Preserve exactly, from the reference image: room shape and proportions; the position, count and size of every wall, window, door and opening; ceiling height 2.7 m; the camera position, angle, field of view and framing; and the zoning of the furniture — every large item stays where its block stands, with the same footprint and orientation. Keep the input aspect ratio; do not crop or re-frame.

Within each block you may replace the placeholder with real furniture of the same category, size and orientation, refine its silhouette to the style below, and add finishing materials, textiles, plants, light fixtures and small lived-in details. Kitchen unit composition, appliance models and mirror shapes may vary within the same footprint.

Style: warm modern minimalism (Organic Modern / warm Japandi) for a family of four with two young children and a dog. Clean architectural lines softened by rounded, organic furniture silhouettes — no sharp corners, no thin spindly legs.

Palette: warm white and light beige/greige walls and ceiling as the base; olive and forest-green accents (cabinetry, textiles); light and medium-dark natural wood tones (chestnut, pine) for furniture and decor. No cold greys, no bright saturated colors, black used only as a small accent (fixtures, hardware, faucets).

Materials: matte HPL cabinet fronts (no gloss); matte engineered-stone or HPL countertops and backsplash; chrome or gunmetal plumbing fixtures; a wide rectangular kitchen sink with a combined main+filtered-water faucet; tile flooring in the hallway and kitchen zone; warm-toned quartz-vinyl (SPC) flooring in living rooms; natural woven jute/sisal rugs. Wood shows its grain under a matte lacquer; stone shows depth in its veining; upholstery reads as a woven weave, never as vinyl.

Furniture: rounded, low-profile, substantial silhouettes; sofa without armrests, deep seat, dense durable upholstery (bouclé or performance-weave fabric) in a warm neutral tone; round or soft-edged coffee tables in wood or stone.

Lighting: layered warm light (~2700K), no single central ceiling fixture — recessed spotlights, integrated LED strip lighting along cabinets, shelves and niches, a few small sconces as accents only. Light comes from the windows and from the fixtures already visible in the reference, falls off towards the far corners, and every object casts a contact shadow where it meets the floor. The view through a window keeps its detail instead of burning out to white.

Decor: minimal and natural — wood and bamboo accessories in chestnut/pine tones, one statement floor plant in a woven basket per zone (fiddle-leaf fig, small palm, or potted orange tree) plus a few smaller plants elsewhere, always clear of doorways and walking paths. No frescoes, no figurines, no moldings or ornate trim, no visual clutter, no readable text or brand logos. A slightly lived-in, realistic level of tidiness is welcome, not a showroom-perfect scene.

Windows: minimal blackout roller blinds mounted tight inside the window recess — no fabric curtains or drapery of any kind.

Camera: 24 mm architectural lens, natural depth of field, no fisheye distortion, sharp across the room.

## r4-window
The same kitchen-living room seen from the north-east corner towards the sofa (camera 4.3). The sofa without armrests stands along the left wall under a framed picture, its back against the walnut slat panel; the corner kitchen is visible in the depth on the right; the edge of the walnut TV panel closes the frame on the right. The doorway to the hall is in the middle of the far wall. Same finishes as the other shots of this room: same cabinet colour, same tile, same oak floor, same slat walnut.
The floor in the foreground stays open — no dining table, no chairs, no coffee table in the walking path.

Image 1 is a finished render of the same flat from another angle. Copy its finishes exactly: the same cabinet colour and fronts, the same floor, worktop, backsplash, wall paint, textiles and light temperature. It is a material reference only — take no geometry from it. The last image is the 3D scene for this shot and the only source of geometry, camera and furniture placement.
